paragraphs: Children in care in Leeds are looked after by Foster4Leeds, the council's own not-for-profit fostering service, and by the independent agencies shown above. The council's sufficiency strategy for 2024 to 2027 recorded 1,548 children in care in March 2024, 7% more than a year before, and said over 60% of its children in care live with Leeds foster carers. Where its own carers cannot meet the need, it finds homes through independent agencies on the White Rose framework.

Foster4Leeds says it is short of carers for young people aged 11 to 17, for large groups of brothers and sisters, and for children who are disabled or have complex needs. The strategy shows why older children matter so much here: in December 2023, 62% of the city's children in care were aged 10 to 17.

Short-term care can last from a few weeks to two years, and the service also recruits emergency, long-term, parent and child and support carers, as well as short-break carers for disabled children, typically one weekend every six weeks. You can apply from 21, though applicants aged 21 to 25 need to show relevant experience or transferable skills; there is no upper age limit, and you need a spare bedroom.

Each Foster4Leeds carer has their own social worker, membership of the Leeds Foster Care Association, The Fostering Network and FosterTalk, monthly support groups and the option of a Mockingbird hub, and the service pays travel and parking for training. Carers get free Active Leeds gym membership, and children in their care free junior gym and swimming lessons. Foster4Leeds sets out a weekly allowance by age and a skills fee for its higher levels on its own site; we have not yet published Leeds rates, so check the current figures with the service and compare them with two or three of the agencies above.

Fostering with the council means caring for Leeds children near their schools and families, with the city's own social workers; an agency assesses and supports you itself and may offer you children from several councils. To start with the council, call Foster4Leeds on 0113 378 3538. The Bradford, Wakefield, York, North Yorkshire and West Yorkshire pages list services nearby.
